script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Comedy
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

TITLE: FRESH BAKED

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

JANE (mid-30s, earnest) stands over a counter, kneading a stubborn ball of dough. Her brow furrows as she works the dough. Her husband, MARK (mid-40s, easygoing), enters the room.

MARK
(cheerful)
Morning, love. Smells like you're making bread again.

JANE
(sighs)
Yes. I can't seem to get it right this time.

MARK
Why don't you let me help?

JANE
(shrugs)
It's just a little...sticky.

MARK rolls up his sleeves and gets to work alongside Jane. They exchange banter as they work.

INT. BAKERY - DAY

Jane and Mark open the doors to their small-town bakery, "Fresh Baked." Customers file in for pastries and loaves of bread. The bell above the door jingles as it closes behind the last customer.

MARK
(satisfied)
Another successful day.

JANE
(smiling)
Yes, but I want to make our bread truly exceptional.

MARK
Well, we can't keep our customers waiting forever.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jane sits at the kitchen table, staring at a stack of unsold loaves. Mark enters the room, carrying a basket of spoiled vegetables from the market.

MARK
(sighs)
Looks like we've got some work to do tonight.

JANE
(disappointed)
I thought I could make a perfect loaf of bread.

MARK
We'll figure it out, Jane. Maybe we need to try a new recipe.

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

Jane and Mark scour the library's cookbook section for a new bread recipe. They laugh and make jokes as they flip through books.

INT. KITCHEN - NIGHT

Jane and Mark work late into the night, experimenting with a new bread recipe. They taste test each loaf and discuss the results.

INT. TOWN SQUARE - DAY

The townspeople gather in the town square for the annual "Bread Festival." Jane and Mark set up their stand with their new bread, nervously anticipating the judges' tasting.

JANE
(anxious)
I hope this is it, Mark.

MARK
(confident)
We've got this, Jane.

The judges sample their bread, and the crowd holds its breath as they discuss their findings.

JUDGE 1
(impressed)
This is truly exceptional bread.

JANE and MARK exchange elated glances.

INT. BAKERY - NIGHT

Jane and Mark celebrate their victory with a bottle of champagne. They toast to their newfound success and the joys of small-town life.

FADE OUT.

THE END
